parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The introduction is the most important part of your report — it is the first thing your reader sees and it must make them WANT to read more.
content: 📖 The introduction is the most important part of your report — it is the first thing your reader sees and it must make them WANT to read more.

A powerful introduction has THREE essential elements. First, the HOOK: one or two sentences that immediately grab attention. The best hooks use a surprising statistic, a thought-provoking question, or a vivid description. Second, BACKGROUND: 2-3 sentences giving context. What is the topic? Why is it important? Third, the THESIS STATEMENT: a clear, confident statement of your main argument or finding. The thesis tells the reader exactly what the report will prove or show.

There are four common hook types: Statistical hook ('1 million tonnes of plastic enter the ocean every day.'), Question hook ('What if all ocean fish disappeared by 2050?'), Fact hook ('The blue whale is the largest animal ever to exist on Earth.'), Scenario hook ('Imagine a world where water is more expensive than gold.').
